summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Workup revealed gastroparesis confirmed by a gastric emptying study showing 85% retention at four hours, and a Campylobacter infection identified on stool culture. She was treated with azithromycin and restarted on metoclopramide at a reduced dose with improvement. A liver biopsy ruled out hepatic GVHD, allowing reduction of prednisone from 17.5 mg to 15 mg daily. Her tachycardia and lightheadedness improved with hydration. She tolerated oral intake, and symptoms resolved prior to discharge. She was discharged home on azithromycin, metoclopramide, prednisone, and continued anticoagulation, with plans for outpatient follow-up.
